# SUMO IS A BOXER — Midnight Bout

A first-person boxing game built entirely on **My Game Engine 1.0**, consumed as
a published package. An evolution of the *IRON PALMS — Midnight Bout* concept.

**Everything you can see was generated by code.** No image, no texture file, no
`.fbx`, `.obj` or `.glb`, no downloaded model, no DCC tool, no asset service.
The warehouse, the ring, the crowd, the opponent and the player's gloves are all
MeshIR authored through the engine's modeling verbs and surfaced through
Material Forge definitions.

---

## Run it

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

Then open **http://127.0.0.1:5180** and click **CLICK TO FIGHT**.

```bash
npm test     # 56 headless tests: assets, scene, combat, input, engine consumption
npm run build
npm run preview
```

## How the fight works

Guard **height** and **bracing** are two different things, and the read between
them is the whole fight.

| Your state when it lands | What gets through |
|---|---|
| Braced, guard at the right height | ~12 %, and your guard meter pays for it |
| Braced, guard at the wrong height | ~60 % |
| Hands up, not braced, right height | ~80 % |
| Neither | all of it |
| Dodging | nothing |

Absorbing blocks drains the **guard meter**. Empty it and the guard **breaks** —
that fighter is open and staggered for a second and a half. Hit an opponent
during its wind-up and you land a **counter** at 1.45×.

Three knockdowns ends it. So does the round clock, on a decision.

## Architecture

```
src/
  main.js                      browser entry
  game/
    config.js                  all fight tuning, one file
    app.js                     boot, fixed-step loop, event -> presentation
    assets/
      kit.js                   MeshIR authoring kit over the engine's verbs
      materials.js             37 Material Forge families, 112 definitions
      ring.js                  platform, canvas, posts, ropes, padding, steps
      warehouse.js             slab, walls, columns, roof, gantry, services, doors
      dressing.js              heavy bags, barriers, bleachers, crowd, clutter
      fighter-kit.js           gloves, trunks, boots, face, first-person arms
    scene/arena-scene.js       the authored SceneDefinition (66 semantic nodes)
    presentation/              asset library, scene presenter, lights, camera, VFX
    character/                 opponent (Character + Motion Forge), player fists
    combat/                    fighters, damage resolution, AI, the match
    input/                     semantic action vocabulary and the router
    audio/                     game-owned Web Audio (see ENGINE_GAPS GAP-11)
    hud/                       DOM fight presentation
engine/                        the engine under test — READ-ONLY
tests/                         56 headless tests
ENGINE_GAPS.md                 16 recorded gaps, with workarounds and ownership
```

### The engine is a dependency, and stays one

Every engine import goes through the published specifier:

```js
import { createSceneDefinition, buildHumanoidCharacter /* … */ }
  from '@sumosizedginger/my-game-engine-1.0/full';
```

`engine/` is a committed subtree and is never modified.
`tests/engine-consumption.test.js` enforces both halves of that: it scans every
import specifier in `src/`, checks every imported name against the live
`engine/full` surface, and asserts `git status --porcelain -- engine` is empty.

### Engine capability actually used

**34 of the engine's 132 public exports**, verified against the live package by
`tests/engine-consumption.test.js` rather than listed by hand.

| Subsystem | Names the game imports |
|---|---|
| **Geometry Forge** | `createMesh` · `createPart` · `createBoxMesh` · `createCylinderMesh` · `extrudeProfile` · `transformMesh` · `mergeMeshIR` · `triangleCount` · `vertexCount` · `createAnchor` |
| **Material Forge** | `createMaterialDefinition` |
| **Character Forge** | `createCharacterDefinition` · `buildHumanoidCharacter` · `resolveHumanoidParameters` · `computeSemanticLandmarks` (plus `bonesByName` on the built result) |
| **Motion Forge** | `createMotionDefinition` · `createLocomotionEvaluator` · `solveTwoBoneIK` · `commitRootMotionIntent` |
| **Scene Composition** | `createSceneDefinition` · `createSceneNode` · `validateSceneDefinition` · `compileScene` · `instantiateScene` |
| **Preview** | `createPreviewable` |
| **Gameplay Foundation** | `createSimulationClock` · `createEntityManager` · `createTransformManager` · `TRANSFORM_OWNERSHIP` · `createStateManager` · `createRuleEngine` · `createInputSystem` |
| **Identity** | `ENGINE_NAME` · `ENGINE_VERSION` |

The tests additionally consume `validateMesh`, `meshHash`, `PREVIEW_BUDGET_DEFAULTS`,
`SCENE_MAX_NODES` and `liveSceneInstanceCount` as verification surface.

### Laws this build keeps

- **The scene is the authored truth.** The venue is a `SceneDefinition` compiled
  to an artifact and instantiated; the Three.js tree is a flat consumer of
  already-composed world matrices and never re-composes a hierarchy.
- **One transform writer per step.** Movement, the AI and the ring constraint all
  produce *intent*; `transforms.commitAll(dt)` is the only writer.
- **Motion produces intent, not position.** `commitRootMotionIntent` writes into
  a game-owned transform. The evaluator never moves anything itself.
- **Input is semantic.** Combat code asks whether `JAB` fired. Exactly one module
  knows a mouse exists.
- **Nothing allocates in the combat loop.** Particles are ring-recycled from
  fixed buffers; materials and geometry are uploaded once and shared; a rematch
  reuses its entities and transforms.

## What is game-owned, and why

Recorded in full in [`ENGINE_GAPS.md`](./ENGINE_GAPS.md) — 16 gaps, each with the
capability attempted, the public API inspected, why it was insufficient, the
legal workaround, and whose fix it is. The short version:

| The game owns | Because |
|---|---|
| Scene → renderer presentation | The engine's adapter is not public (GAP-01) |
| `revolve`, `roundedBox`, `tube`, `chain` | The verb set is box/cylinder/extrude (GAP-02) |
| Seeded RNG | No public random service, though the law requires one (GAP-05) |
| Boxing poses, guard, punches, knockdown | Motion Forge has one clip and no blending (GAP-09) |
| Particles | No VFX subsystem (GAP-10) |
| All audio | **No audio subsystem exists at all** (GAP-11) |
| Renderer, camera, lights | No public presentation surface (GAP-14) |
| Ring and fighter collision | Runtime collision is Pong-specific (GAP-15) |
